title: Miami or Lima: who is further west?
hook: Peru faces the Pacific and Florida the Atlantic. Which city is further west?

knows: that South America is south of North America
that a meridian is a line of longitude
doesNotKnow: that South America also lies well to the east
that Miami's meridian meets South America on the Pacific side

misconception: Lima, Peru is far west of Miami because it faces the Pacific.
objective: The learner can say that Miami (80.2 W) is further west than Lima (77.0 W), and that Miami's meridian runs south through Cuba, Panama, Ecuador and Peru.

claims.text: Miami is at 80.2°W and Lima at 77.0°W, so Miami is 3.1° further west.
claims.source: From memory, not re-checked: gazetteer values Miami 25.7617 N 80.1918 W, Lima 12.0464 S 77.0428 W (the brief gives 80.19 and 77.04). Difference 3.149 degrees; the stage shows it to one decimal as 3.1.

claims.text: Miami's meridian runs south through Cuba, Panama, Ecuador and Peru.
claims.source: Builder's node walk (0.1 degree steps, d3-geoContains over the kit's 1:110m countries) along -80.1918 from 30 N to 18 S: United States, Cuba, Panama, Ecuador, Peru (Ecuador and Peru alternate near 4 S). Ocean stretches between them are not named. Resolution caveat: borders are coarse and small islands missing, so the list is for this data, not a border claim.

claims.text: Apart from the coastal tips of Ecuador and Peru, South America lies east of Miami's meridian.
claims.source: Builder's node check of country bounds in the kit's 1:110m data: Peru's western edge is 81.41 W and Ecuador's 80.97 W (both west of 80.19 W); Colombia's is 78.99 W; every other South American country lies further east. Galapagos islands are absent from the data and not claimed.

claims.text: On an equirectangular map, the x position is proportional to longitude, so a meridian is a vertical line.
claims.source: Snyder (1987), Map Projections: A Working Manual. From memory, not re-checked. Stage is labelled equirectangular.

claims.text: Peru faces the Pacific and Florida faces the Atlantic.
claims.source: Hook. Common geography: Peru's coast is on the Pacific Ocean; Florida's east coast is on the Atlantic (its west coast on the Gulf of Mexico). From memory.

recall.question: Is Lima, Peru east or west of Miami?
recall.why: Miami is at about 80.2 W and Lima about 77.0 W, so Lima is slightly east of Miami.
